title: Galois-invariant closed subsets of the base change descend to the ground scheme
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a possibly infinite Galois extension k-bar/k, a k-scheme X and a closed subset T-bar of X_k-bar that is stable under every sigma in Gal(k-bar/k), and asks for a closed subset T of X whose inverse image is T-bar (statement lines 900-909). After the reduction to X = Spec(A) the proof has to descend a radical ideal I-bar of the infinite tensor product A ⊗_k k-bar along the Galois action, and the two steps that are not formal are the finiteness reduction - an arbitrary x in I-bar already lies in A ⊗_k k' for some finite Galois subextension k'/k, so that the orbit polynomial P(T) = prod_{sigma in G}(T - sigma(x)) can be formed and is monic of degree |G| (proof lines 918-923) - and the identification of the invariants of that finite stage with A, which puts all coefficients a_i into A and hence, by sigma-invariance of I-bar, into I = A cap I-bar (proof lines 924-927). Only then does P(x) = 0 yield x^d in I(A ⊗_k k-bar), i.e. membership in a radical, which is what turns Galois invariance into an actual descent statement for closed subsets (proof lines 928-931).
